title: Respiratory Restriction Leaded by Conventional or Minimally Invasive Sugical Repair of Oesophageal Atresia in Children
official: Assessment of Respiratory Restriction Caused by Chest Wall Abnormalities Following Conventional or Minimal Invasive Surgical Repair of Type III Esophageal Atresia in School Age Children
summary:
Children born with esophageal atresia need surgery shortly after birth. For many years, the standard operation was a thoracotomy, an opening in the chest that can sometimes lead to changes in the shape of the chest wall. Although these changes are visible on X rays, doctors still do not fully understand how much they affect breathing later in childhood. A newer, less invasive technique called thoracoscopy uses small incisions and appears to cause fewer chest deformities, but its impact on lung function has not yet been clearly established.

This study aims to compare the breathing capacity of children aged 6 to 9 who were operated on using either thoracotomy or thoracoscopy. The main question is whether one group is more likely to develop restrictive lung syndrome, a condition in which the lungs cannot expand normally. To answer this, the study relies on lung function tests and chest X rays performed during routine follow up visits.

Beyond this primary goal, the study also examines other possible breathing problems, the presence of chest wall abnormalities, and factors that might influence lung health, such as nutrition, physical activity, associated malformations, and overall quality of life.

A total of at least 360 children across France will participate. They are identified through national registries and invited during scheduled follow up consultations.
criteria:
For thoracoscopy group:

Inclusion Criteria:

* Child operated on by thoracoscopy for type 3 AO (excluding long gap) according to Ladd's classification
* Child aged 6 to 10 years old
* Consent from parents (or legal guardians) and the child's agreement to participate in the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Heart or lung malformation diagnosed at birth and requiring surgery
* Conversion from thoracoscopy to thoracotomy during the procedure
* Child who has had more than one thoracic surgery (reoperation for AO, other reasons for thoracic surgery including heart surgery)
* For Thoracotomy group\*:

Inclusion Criteria :

--Child operated on by thoracotomy for type 3 AO (excluding long gap) according to the Ladd classification

* Child aged 6 to 10 years old
* Consent from parents (or legal guardians) and the child's agreement to participate in the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Heart or lung malformation diagnosed at birth and requiring surgery
* Child who has had more than one thoracic surgery (reoperation for AO, other reason for thoracic surgery including heart surgery)
* Child operated on for type 3 AO via thoracotomy (excluding long gap) according to Ladd's classification

For each patient who underwent thoracoscopic surgery included in the study, two patients who had thoracotomy, matched according to known or suspected confounding factors for restrictive syndromes from the RestriMIS1 (NCT04136795) study\*\*, will be included.

\*It's possible that some children had multiple consecutive surgeries. In those cases, if one of the procedures was a thoracotomy, the children will be classified in the thoracotomy group (the more major surgery).

\*\*Prematurity, birth weight, presence of tracheomalacia, and GERD during the neonatal period (clinically and/or on additional tests)
